extracted.intended_audience: FOIA officers, requesters, and submitters interacting with the Commission's FOIA process
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing the Commission's handling of FOIA requests, including notices, confidentiality of commercial information, appeals, preservation, fee assessments, payments, and related rights and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response timing and interim/rolling releases
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request involves a voluminous amount of material, or searches in multiple locations, the agency may provide interim responses, releasing the records on a rolling basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will provide an estimated date by which it expects to provide a response to the requester. For voluminous or multi-location searches, interim or rolling releases are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant notice content and track assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a FOIA Officer grants a request, in full or in part, the Commission shall promptly provide the requester written notice of the decision, what fees apply under section 10 of this subpart, and the availability of its FOIA Public Liaison to offer assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must also inform the requester whether the request has been assigned to the Standard, Complex, or Expedited track pursuant to § 426.205(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes a denial and required denial notice contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A denial of request includes decisions that: fees will not be waived, no expedited processing will be done, there are no responsive records subject to FOIA, the requested record does not exist or has been destroyed, the requested record is exempt in whole or in part, or the request does not reasonably describe the records sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When denying a request in any respect, the Commission will notify the requester in writing and the written notice will include: (1) the name and title/position of the person responsible for the denial; (2) a brief statement of the reasons for the denial, including any FOIA exemption applied; (3) a description of the material withheld (approximate pages or other reasonable estimation); (4) a statement that the denial may be appealed under section 8(a) of this subpart and description of appeal requirements; and (5) a statement notifying the requester of assistance available from the FOIA Public Liaison and OGIS dispute resolution services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction annotation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When a portion of a record is withheld, the amount of information redacted and the claimed exemption will be noted at the place in the record where the redaction was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redactions should indicate both the extent of withheld information and which exemption(s) are being claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of confidential commercial information (CCI) and submitter
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential commercial information means commercial or financial information obtained by the Commission from a submitter that may be protected from disclosure under Exemption 4 of the FOIA, 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4). Submitter means any person or entity (including corporations, States, or foreign governments, but not another Federal Government entity) that provides CCI, directly or indirectly, to the Federal Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of CCI at time of submission and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: A submitter of confidential commercial information must use good faith efforts to designate by appropriate markings, at the time of submission, any portion of its submission that it considers to be protected from disclosure under Exemption 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These designations expire 10 years after the date of the submission unless the submitter requests and provides justification for a longer designation period.

rubrics_metrics.name: When notice to submitters is required
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must promptly provide written notice to the submitter of confidential commercial information whenever records containing such information are requested under the FOIA if the agency determines that it may be required to disclose the records, provided the requested information has been designated in good faith by the submitter or the Commission has reason to believe that the requested information may be protected from disclosure under Exemption 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must either describe the commercial information requested or include a copy of the requested records or portions of records containing the information. For voluminous numbers of submitters, the Commission may post or publish notice in a place/manner reasonably likely to inform submitters instead of sending individual notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to submitter-notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice requirements do not apply if: (1) The Commission determines the information is exempt and will not be disclosed; (2) The information has been lawfully published or officially made available to the public; (3) Disclosure is required by a statute other than FOIA or by a regulation issued in accordance with Exec. Order 12,600; or (4) The submitter's designation appears obviously frivolous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If designation appears frivolous and the Commission intends to disclose, the Commission must give the submitter written notice of any final decision to disclose within a reasonable number of days prior to a specified disclosure date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitter opportunity to object and substance of objections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must specify a reasonable time period within which the submitter must respond to notice. If a submitter objects to disclosure, it should provide a detailed written statement specifying all grounds for withholding the particular information under any FOIA exemption. To rely on Exemption 4, the submitter must explain why the information constitutes a trade secret or commercial/financial information that is confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond within the specified time is considered no objection; the Commission is not required to consider information received after the date of any disclosure decision; any information provided by a submitter may itself be subject to disclosure. The Commission must consider a submitter’s objections and specific grounds in deciding whether to disclose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of intent to disclose over submitter objection
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the Commission decides to disclose information over the objection of a submitter, the agency must provide the submitter written notice which must include: (1) a statement of the reasons why each of the submitter’s disclosure objections was not sustained; (2) a description of the information to be disclosed or copies of the records as the Commission intends to release them; and (3) a specified disclosure date, which must be a reasonable time after the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when FOIA lawsuit is filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a requester files a lawsuit seeking to compel the disclosure of confidential commercial information, the Commission must promptly notify the submitter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester notification regarding submitter notices and lawsuits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must notify the requester whenever it provides the submitter with notice and an opportunity to object to disclosure; whenever it notifies the submitter of its intent to disclose the requested information; and whenever a submitter files a lawsuit to prevent the disclosure of the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for administrative appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester may appeal an initial determination of the Commission, including but not limited to determinations: (1) to deny access to records in whole or in part; (2) to assign a particular fee category; (3) to deny a request for reduction or waiver of fees; (4) that no records could be located that are responsive; or (5) to deny a request for expedited processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiating appeals: form, timing, and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters not satisfied may make a written appeal within 90 days of the FOIA Officer’s decision. Appeals should be clearly marked 'Freedom of Information Act Appeal' and may be submitted via email, website, or mail. The request should set out requester name and contact information, specify date of initial request and initial determination, and set forth why the appeal should be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailing address and email (FOIA@inspire2serve.gov) are provided; advisable to send via email due to mail delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication of appeals and judicial review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals will be processed in order of receipt. An appeal ordinarily will not be adjudicated if the request becomes a matter of FOIA litigation. Before seeking review by a court of an agency’s adverse determination, a requester generally must first submit a timely administrative appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal decision timing and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission’s Chair or designee shall decide whether to affirm or reverse the initial determination (in whole or in part), and shall notify the requester of this decision in writing within 20 work days, pursuant to § 426.205(c). If the appeal is denied, the Commission will notify the requester in writing of the decision, the reasons for the denial (including FOIA exemptions relied upon), the name and title of the official responsible, and provisions for judicial review and OGIS. If the appeal is granted in full or in part, the Chief FOIA Officer will notify the requester in writing and promptly process the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute resolution participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Dispute resolution is a voluntary process. If the Commission agrees to participate in OGIS dispute resolution, it will actively engage as a partner to the process in an attempt to resolve the dispute. Requesters may seek dispute resolution by contacting the FOIA Public Liaison or OGIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OGIS contact information is provided (email ogis@nara.gov; telephone/fax/toll-free numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of FOIA request records
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will preserve all correspondence pertaining to the requests that it receives under this subpart, as well as copies of all requested records, until disposition or destruction is authorized pursuant to title 44 of the United States Code or the General Records Schedule 4.2 of NARA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will not dispose of or destroy records while they are the subject of a pending request, appeal, or lawsuit under the FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee policy overview and requester categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall charge the requester for processing a request under the FOIA in accordance with this section and with the OMB Guidelines. For assessing fees, FOIA establishes three categories of requesters: commercial use requesters; non-commercial scientific or educational institutions or news media requesters; and all other requesters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters may seek a fee waiver; the Commission will consider fee waiver requests under paragraph (f). No fees are charged if total fees incurred are below $25. Payments by check/money order to the U.S. Treasury or other Commission-determined methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key fee-related definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial use request: seeks information to further a commercial, trade, or profit interest (including litigation). Direct costs: expenses incurred in searching for and duplicating (and for commercial requests, reviewing) records, e.g., employee salary (basic rate plus 16%) and equipment costs; excludes overhead. Duplication: reproducing records into copies (paper, audiovisual, electronic). Educational institution: any school operating a program of scholarly research; must show request is in connection with role. Noncommercial scientific institution: operated solely for scientific research not intended to promote a product/industry. Representative of the news media: entity that gathers information of potential public interest, edits it into a distinct work, and distributes it to the public; includes internet-only news organizations; freelancers with solid expectation of publication may qualify. Review: examination of a record to determine whether any portion is exempt; includes redaction and considering formal objections from CCI submitters but not general legal/policy issue resolution. Search: looking for and retrieving responsive records; includes page-by-page identification and reasonable efforts for electronic records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided (professor of geology scenarios) illustrate educational vs non-educational uses and demonstrate that stated purpose matters over stationery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees chargeable for specific services (duplication, search, review, inspection, other)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will charge fees for copying records ($0.12 per page up to 8½ x 14; actual cost for photos/films/other materials; scanning costs passed to requester), search services (charge for all time spent searching even if no responsive records), review of records (only charged to commercial use requesters; charged at employee salary rate plus 16% for those performing review), inspection of records in reading room (fees charged for services; no fee for monitoring inspection in physical reading room), and other special services (charged at actual cost, e.g., certifying true copies or express mailing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For electronic records, search charges are the actual direct cost (computer search time, runs, operator salary). Review fees are not charged at administrative appeal stage; re-review costs may be assessed if an exemption no longer applies and additional review is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees applicable by requester category
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial use requesters: charged the full direct cost of searching for, reviewing, and duplicating records. Educational and non-commercial scientific requesters: charged only duplication costs, with first 100 pages (or equivalent) provided free; must show records sought are for scholarly research and not commercial use. News media: charged only duplication costs with first 100 pages (or equivalent) free. Other requesters: charged full direct cost of searching and duplicating, but first 100 pages of duplication and first two hours of search time are provided free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will advise requesters of their placement in these categories and may seek verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances when fees are not charged or are excused
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may not charge a requester a fee if the total fee is equal to or less than $25. Additionally, the Commission may not charge search or duplication fees if it fails to comply with time limits under §§ 426.205 or 426.208, unless: (1) a court has determined exceptional circumstances exist; (2) the Commission has determined unusual circumstances apply and provided timely written notice in accordance with § 426.205(d) (time limit excused for additional 10 days); or (3) unusual circumstances apply, more than 5,000 pages are necessary, timely written notice provided, and the Commission discussed scope-limiting options with requester (or made three good-faith attempts) — then the Commission may charge applicable fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and process for waiver or reduction of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester may request a waiver or reduction of fees in writing during the initial FOIA request. The waiver must demonstrate that the fee reduction or waiver is in the public interest because it furnishes information likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of government operations or activities, and the information is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine satisfaction, the Commission will consider whether: the subject has a direct connection to government operations or activities; the disclosable portion is meaningfully informative and not already public; disclosure would contribute to understanding of a reasonably broad audience (not just the individual requester); and the public's understanding would be significantly enhanced. The Commission will also consider any commercial interest of the requester and weigh public interest magnitude against identified commercial interest. Partial waivers may be granted for portions that qualify. The Commission must notify the requester of its determination. If denied, the denial notification must advise that processing will not continue unless requester directs and agrees to pay fees or sets an upper limit (not less than $25); failure to respond in 30 days will be deemed withdrawal; denial may be appealed under § 426.208.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of estimated fees and tolling of processing
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency estimates fees will exceed $25, it must notify the requester of the actual or estimated amount with a breakdown of fees for search, review, or duplication, unless requester indicated willingness to pay anticipated fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester does not commit in writing to pay (or designate an amount or statutory entitlement for noncommercial requesters), the request will not be considered received and work will not continue. If only part of fee can be estimated, the Commission will advise accordingly. If requester indicated willingness to pay a designated amount but estimate exceeds that amount, processing is tolled while the Commission inquires whether the requester wishes to revise payment amount or modify the request; processing resumes when requester responds. The FOIA Public Liaison is available to assist in reformulating requests to lower cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance payment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally the Commission will not require advance payment before work is commenced. However, when the Commission determines or estimates total fees will exceed $250, it may require advance payment up to the entire anticipated fee before beginning processing. The agency may elect to process prior to collecting fees if it receives satisfactory assurance of full payment from a requester with history of prompt payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a requester previously failed to pay a fee within 30 calendar days of billing, the requester must pay the full amount owed plus applicable interest and make an advance payment of the full estimated fee before the Commission begins to process a new request. If advance payment is required, the request is not considered received until payment is received; failure to pay within 30 calendar days will result in the request being closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging interest on unpaid bills and debt collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may charge interest on any unpaid bill starting on the 31st day following the date of billing. Interest charges will be assessed at the rate provided in 31 U.S.C. 3717 and will accrue from the billing date until payment is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will follow the provisions of the Debt Collection Act of 1982 and its administrative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregating multiple requests to prevent fee avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission reasonably determines that a requester or a group of requesters acting together is attempting to divide a request into a series of requests to avoid fees, the Commission may aggregate those requests and charge accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may presume multiple related requests submitted within a 30-calendar-day period are intended to avoid fees. For requests separated by longer periods, aggregation will occur only where there is reasonable basis. The Commission shall not aggregate multiple requests involving unrelated matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of other fee statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee schedule of this section does not apply to fees charged under any statute that specifically requires an agency to set and collect fees for particular types of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where records responsive to a request are subject to a statutorily-based fee schedule program, the Commission must inform the requester of the contact information for that program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other rights and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this subpart shall be construed to entitle any person, as of right, to any service or to the disclosure of any record to which such person is not entitled under the FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and provision of auxiliary aids (Part 457 context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary aids means services or devices that enable persons with impaired sensory, manual, or speaking skills to have an equal opportunity to participate in, and enjoy the benefits of, programs or activities conducted by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include readers, brailled materials, audio recordings, telecommunications devices and other similar services/devices for vision impairment; for hearing impairment examples include TDDs, telephone handset amplifiers, telephones compatible with hearing aids, telecommunication devices for deaf persons (TDDs), interpreters, notetakers, written materials, and other similar services and devices.
